record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let L*_n be the height of DTCS(n), meaning the maximum number of edges on a root-to-leaf path in the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree on n leaves. Prove that L*_n / log^2 n converges in probability to a constant c, and determine that constant.

evidence.quote: Write L∗_n and Ln for the tree height and the height of a random leaf in DTCS(n).
Open Problem 4 Show that L∗_n ∼ c log2 n in probability, and identify the constant c.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree on n leaves, DTCS(n), recursively as follows. For n = 1 the tree is a single leaf. For n ≥ 2, choose a random split size I_n ∈ {1, 2, …, n−1} with distribution
   P(I_n = i) = (1/h_{n−1}) · n / (2 i (n − i)),  i = 1, …, n−1,
where h_{n−1} = ∑_{j=1}^{n−1} 1/j is the (n−1)-st harmonic number. Attach two edges from a root to the roots of two independent subtrees distributed as DTCS(I_n) and DTCS(n − I_n), respectively. Let L*_n denote the height of DTCS(n), i.e. the maximum number of edges on any path from the root to a leaf.

Prove that there exists a constant c ∈ (0, ∞) such that
   L*_n / (log n)^2  →  c  in probability  as n → ∞,
and determine the value of c explicitly.
artifact.status_search_result: Available work on the critical beta-splitting model (notably the Aldous–Pittel analysis of heights and subsequent papers via contraction and Mellin analysis) establishes sharp asymptotics and central limit theorems for the height L_n of a uniform random leaf, with L_n/(log n)^2 → 6/π^2 in probability, and provides tail bounds for the maximum leaf height L*_n. However, the precise in-probability limit L*_n/(log n)^2 → c with an explicitly identified constant c does not appear to have been proven; the problem remains listed as open in subsequent literature, with only upper and lower tail bounds known.

status_evidence.title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree: Heights and Related Results
status_evidence.snippet: We give tail bounds for the time-height and the edge-height of the tree, that is the maximal leaf heights.
status_evidence.claim: Only tail bounds (not a precise limiting constant) are established for the maximum leaf height L*_n.

status_evidence.title: Critical beta-splitting, via contraction
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent work analyzes the leaf-height L_n via the contraction method, refining its distributional limits.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work refines results for the leaf height L_n but does not resolve the maximum height L*_n limit.

status_evidence.title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree IV: Mellin analysis of Leaf Height
status_evidence.snippet: Mellin analysis sharpening the asymptotic distribution of the leaf height.
status_evidence.claim: Continued investigation of leaf-height asymptotics, while the tree-height limiting constant is not identified.
